description: Further expansion of the Vessel Monitoring System for Multi-Day Fishing Vessels and IDAY Fishing Vessels in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-06 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - A major challenge faced by Sri Lanka, as well as many fishing nations around the world, is suppression of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing and other unlawful activities carried out using fishing vessels including drug trafficking, human trafficking, and the transport of illegal cargo. Various measures have been taken at the local, regional and international levels to combat this situation. At the regional level, Sri Lanka is a member of the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission, and according to the rules of the Commission, every fishing vessel engaged in international waters are required to be continuously monitored by the Vessel Monitoring System (VMS). Currently, out of the 5,200 registered multi-day fishing vessels operating in Sri Lanka, 4,200 multi-day fishing vessels have been equipped with monitoring systems, which were received as a Grant from the Australian Government. Since it is mandatory to install VMS for every newly registered multi-day fishing vessel after 2021-01-01, vessel owners purchase and install VMS equipment in vessels registered from that date. There are approximately 1,500 multi-day fishing vessels and IDAY fishing vessels without VMS that were registered as multi-day fishing vessels before 2021-01-01 and are operating in domestic waters and sometimes in international waters. Of these, 400 vessels with a length of more than 34 feet can be used for fishing or other activities in international waters at any time. In addition, remaining 1,100 vessels are those that do not have sufficient technical suitability to remain at sea for extended periods, given their engine capacity and fuel capacity. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Fisheries, Aquatic and Ocean Resources to make it mandatory for those 1,500 vessels to install appropriate monitoring systems and for the Government to bear the cost thereof, was approved by the Cabinet.
